E4 · Role of the tutor (Egyptian)

First part, informal (3 minutes). The tutor is an Egyptian colleague: izzayyak? il-usbūʿ ʿadda izzāy? Then he comments on a news report: šuft ḫabar asʿār tazākir il-ʾaṭr? ʿalit tāni! The student tells his week (at least one episode) and reacts to the news with an opinion. Second part, register read (3 minutes). The tutor passes to the register of a meeting: ana šāyif inn-in nʿmil id- dawra kullaha online, ʿašān nwaffar il-maṣarīf. The student recognizes the advantage, expresses a reservation with grace (ʿandi taḥaffuẓ basīṭ…, maʿa ḥtirāmi li-raʾy ḥaḍritak...) and proposes an alternative (for example a mixed system: mumkin nbuṣṣ ʿa-l-mawḍūʿ Min zawya tanya? yōm fi l-maktab w yomēn Online). The tutor accepts in part.
